Okay, so I need to get an amendment package together for our animal care and use committee and I'd like help drafting it. Background: we run a long-term fish population monitoring program, roughly three to five million fish a year plus some amphibian work, and it's up for five-year protocol renewal. Standard procedures — fin clips, coded wire tags, PIT tag insertion, occasional gill biopsies — almost all of it streamside, no anesthesia, fish back in the water in under a minute. The last protocol had these under the higher pain/distress category, which drags in anesthesia requirements, vet sign-off on every procedure type, tag-size caps, and a public reporting line item, and honestly it's cost us entire field seasons. Our field lead, who has run this program for about twenty-five years and is retiring after this cycle, wants it moved to the momentary-or-slight category on the grounds that most neighboring states classify it that way, that field anesthesia actually raises mortality, and that fish physiology doesn't support the higher tier to begin with. I'll be candid that I think this whole tier system is compliance theater imported from rodent labs, and the science it's slowing down is what keeps thousands of stream miles from getting dewatered, which matters for a lot more animals than the ones we handle. What I need is the amendment itself, a justification memo the committee can act on without a lot of back-and-forth, and a page of talking points for me since I'll be the one presenting it...
